package_info.why_malicious: This article does not describe a specific malicious package, but rather outlines operational risk factors in open-source software supply chains that can lead to security issues. These risks are not always captured by CVEs and include end-of-life status, outdated versions, infrequent updates, and inactive project communities. Such conditions can make software vulnerable to exploitation or unpatched security flaws.

execution_context.trigger: During project maintenance or dependency review

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Component is marked as End-of-Life or has not received updates for over 40 months.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During project maintenance or dependency review, the component is identified as end-of-life or unmaintained, resulting in no further security patches or updates being applied, which allows known and unknown vulnerabilities to persist in the codebase.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: End-of-life or unmaintained components are not monitored for new vulnerabilities and will not receive security patches, leaving any discovered issues unaddressed.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Standard practice expects open-source components to be actively maintained and patched; end-of-life components are abandoned and pose ongoing security risks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Archival of legacy software for historical or research purposes, not for use in production environments.
key_indicators: End-of-life status explicitly stated in project documentation or repository
No updates or releases for over 40 months

execution_context.trigger: During project maintenance or dependency review

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Component version is more than 40 months old or lags 6+ releases behind the latest.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During project maintenance or dependency review, the component is found to be significantly outdated, either by age or by number of releases behind, which increases the likelihood of unpatched vulnerabilities and incompatibility with current security standards.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Outdated versions are less likely to have received recent security fixes and may depend on other outdated, potentially vulnerable components.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Best practices dictate using up-to-date versions; using very old versions increases exposure to known vulnerabilities.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legacy systems with strict compatibility requirements that prevent upgrading to newer versions.
key_indicators: Component is 6 or more releases behind the latest available version
Dependency tree includes other outdated components

execution_context.trigger: During project maintenance or dependency review

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Component has fewer than 2 releases per year, fewer than 100 commits per year, or fewer than 5 unique contributors per year.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During project maintenance or dependency review, the component is identified as having low project activity, such as infrequent releases, few commits, or minimal contributor engagement, which reduces oversight and increases the risk that vulnerabilities will go unnoticed and unpatched.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Low activity suggests the project is not actively maintained, making it less likely that vulnerabilities will be discovered and fixed in a timely manner.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Healthy open-source projects typically have regular releases, frequent commits, and multiple active contributors to ensure ongoing security and code quality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Small, niche projects with limited scope or stable, mature codebases that require minimal changes.
key_indicators: Fewer than 5 unique contributors per year

attack_chain.action: Component is selected for use despite being end-of-life, outdated, or inactive.
attack_chain.leads_to: Increased risk of unpatched vulnerabilities and potential exploitation.

attack_chain.action: Vulnerabilities in the component remain unpatched due to lack of maintenance.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attackers exploit known or unknown vulnerabilities in production environments.

behavioral_signatures: Use of end-of-life or unmaintained components as dependencies
Component versions older than 40 months in dependency manifests
Components lagging 6 or more releases behind the latest available version
Projects with fewer than 2 releases, 100 commits, or 5 contributors per year, as shown in repository metadata
file_indicators: SBOM entries with version numbers older than 40 months
Dependency manifest files (e.g., package.json, requirements.txt, Gemfile.lock) referencing outdated or end-of-life components
Lack of recent commit or release metadata in repository (e.g., no commits or releases in over 40 months)
network_indicators: N/A (operational risk, not runtime network behavior)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Regularly scan your SBOM and dependency manifests for components that are end-of-life, have not been updated in over 40 months, lag 6 or more releases behind the latest, or show low project activity (fewer than 2 releases, 100 commits, or 5 contributors per year). Use automated tools (e.g., JFrog Xray, Snyk, or custom scripts) to enforce policy rules and flag risky components for review or replacement. Integrate repository metadata analysis to identify inactive or abandoned projects.
